reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify baseline patterns across misclassified instances with external XAI tools to quantify feature importance and detect spurious correlations. This approach ensures both intuitive insight and rigorous attribution analysis, especially critical when dealing with tabular data where spurious features may appear subtle or non-semantic.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features are present in all misclassified instances (13590 and 35183) and are not semantically aligned with income prediction (e.g., workclass, occupation, relationship, etc.)
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared features that appear in both instances and lack direct relevance to income class

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any shared feature (e.g., marital-status=Married-civ-spouse, education=HS-grad) could act as a spurious signal due to co-occurrence with misclassification, despite lacking causal or predictive relevance
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A reasoned hypothesis about the spurious nature of the shared feature(s)

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides a robust, game-theoretic attribution of feature importance across all instances, with intersection comparison highlighting features with high shared impact. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local interpretability to confirm how features influence predictions. Sensitivity analysis isolates the effect of each feature being removed, confirming spuriousness. Together, they validate whether high attribution scores correlate with non-semantic features across misclassified cases.
